beliefs: f reverses the order of characters in the string [E1]
f then swaps the case of each letter (upper<->lower), leaving non-letters unchanged [E1, E3]
The case swap is applied to the reversed string, not the original [E3]
The first output character is the case-swapped last input character shifted back by 2 alphabetically within its own case (a->y, A->Y, wrapping z->x, Z->X) [E4, E5, E6, E11]
Non-ASCII Latin-1 letters are case-swapped and shifted back by 2 within their contiguous letter block, skipping the ×/÷ gaps [E12, E13]
The -2 shift applies only when the last character is a letter; otherwise the first output char is just the reversed last char [E8, E9]
The uppercase Latin-1 block is 0xC0..0xDE excluding ×(0xD7), with plain codepoint-2 skipping × (Ñ→Ï, Ó→Ñ, Ö→Ò, Ø→Ö, Þ→Ü) [E19, E20, E23]
À(0xC0) wraps to ¾(0xBE) and Á(0xC1) to ¿(0xBF), so the wrap base is 0xBE extending the block down to ¾ [E16, E19]
The lowercase Latin-1 block is 0xE0..0xFE excluding ÷(0xF7), with plain codepoint-2 skipping ÷ (á→ß, à→Þ, ÿ→ý) [E21, E22]
à(0xE0) wraps to Þ(0xDE) and á(0xE1) to ß(0xDF), so the wrap base is 0xDE extending the block down to Þ [E14, E21, E22]
notes: E23 shows Ø(0xD8)→Ö(0xD6) and Ù(0xD9)→×, i.e. plain codepoint-2 skipping ×, not the 0xBE-based block. So the uppercase shift is plain codepoint-2 skipping ×, with only the À/Á wrap going to ¾/¿. Fixed predict() to use plain arithmetic for uppercase (and lowercase) instead of index-based block lookup, keeping the special À/Á (and à/á) wrap.
